questions.question: Which nutrient is the body's main source of energy?
questions.correctAnswer: Carbohydrates
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are broken down into glucose, the body's main fuel.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Carbs are the body's main fuel.

questions.question: Which nutrient builds and repairs body tissues?
questions.correctAnswer: Protein
questions.explanation: Protein provides amino acids to build and repair muscles and tissues.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Protein builds and repairs the body.

questions.question: Which vitamin does sunlight help the body make?
questions.correctAnswer: Vitamin D
questions.explanation: Sunlight on skin triggers vitamin D production.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sunshine makes vitamin D in your skin.

questions.question: Which food group is the best source of calcium?
questions.correctAnswer: Dairy foods like milk and yogurt
questions.explanation: Dairy products are rich in calcium for bones and teeth.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Milk and yogurt build strong bones.

questions.question: How many cups of water should teens aim to drink each day?
questions.correctAnswer: About 8 cups (64 ounces), more when active
questions.explanation: Teens need roughly 8 cups of water a day, more in heat or exercise.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Eight cups a day keeps you hydrated.

questions.question: What is fiber good for?
questions.correctAnswer: Healthy digestion and feeling full
questions.explanation: Fiber keeps digestion moving and helps you feel full.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fiber keeps your digestion on track.

questions.question: Which type of fat is considered the healthiest?
questions.correctAnswer: Unsaturated fat
questions.explanation: Unsaturated fats from plants, fish, and nuts support heart health.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Unsaturated fats are the heart-friendly ones.

questions.question: What is the main problem with trans fats?
questions.correctAnswer: They raise bad cholesterol and lower good cholesterol
questions.explanation: Trans fats raise LDL cholesterol and lower HDL, increasing heart disease risk.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Trans fats are the worst for your heart.

questions.question: What does the body use iron for?
questions.correctAnswer: Making hemoglobin to carry oxygen in blood
questions.explanation: Iron is needed to make hemoglobin, which carries oxygen in red blood cells.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Iron helps your blood carry oxygen.

questions.question: Which foods are good sources of iron?
questions.correctAnswer: Red meat, beans, and leafy greens
questions.explanation: Iron is found in meat, beans, spinach, and fortified foods.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Beans and spinach are iron-rich.

questions.question: What is a calorie?
questions.correctAnswer: A unit of energy in food
questions.explanation: A calorie measures the energy food provides.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A calorie is a unit of food energy.

questions.question: What is the difference between whole grains and refined grains?
questions.correctAnswer: Whole grains keep the bran, germ, and endosperm; refined grains lose the bran and germ
questions.explanation: Whole grains keep all parts of the grain, including fiber and nutrients.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Whole grains keep the whole grain.

questions.question: What is the best source of vitamin C?
questions.correctAnswer: Citrus fruits, peppers, and broccoli
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is abundant in citrus fruits, bell peppers, and broccoli.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Oranges and peppers are packed with vitamin C.

questions.question: What does protein provide that carbs and fats do not?
questions.correctAnswer: Amino acids for building tissue
questions.explanation: Protein supplies amino acids, the building blocks for muscles, enzymes, and more.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Protein supplies the building blocks.

questions.question: How much of your plate should be fruits and vegetables?
questions.correctAnswer: About half
questions.explanation: MyPlate recommends filling about half your plate with fruits and vegetables.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Half your plate should be fruits and veggies.

questions.question: What is the main risk of eating too much sodium?
questions.correctAnswer: High blood pressure
questions.explanation: Too much sodium raises blood pressure, increasing heart and stroke risk.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Too much salt raises blood pressure.

questions.question: What is a serving of vegetables roughly equal to?
questions.correctAnswer: About 1 cup raw or 1/2 cup cooked
questions.explanation: A standard vegetable serving is about 1 cup raw or half a cup cooked.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: One cup raw is a serving of veggies.

questions.question: Which drink is healthiest?
questions.correctAnswer: Water
questions.explanation: Water hydrates without sugar or calories.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Water is the healthiest drink.

questions.question: What is the main ingredient in most sports drinks?
questions.correctAnswer: Water with sugar and electrolytes
questions.explanation: Sports drinks are mostly water with sugar and salts to replace what sweat loses.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sports drinks replace water and salts.

questions.question: What is anemia?
questions.correctAnswer: A condition where blood lacks enough healthy red blood cells
questions.explanation: Anemia means too few red blood cells or too little hemoglobin, often from low iron.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Anemia means your blood is short on red cells.

questions.question: What is the glycemic index?
questions.correctAnswer: A measure of how quickly a food raises blood sugar
questions.explanation: The glycemic index ranks foods by how fast they raise blood glucose.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: High glycemic foods spike blood sugar fast.

questions.question: Which nutrient is needed in the largest amount each day?
questions.correctAnswer: Water
questions.explanation: Water is the nutrient needed in the largest quantity for hydration and body functions.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Water is your biggest daily need.

questions.question: What is the function of calcium?
questions.correctAnswer: Building strong bones and teeth
questions.explanation: Calcium builds and maintains bones and teeth and helps muscles and nerves work.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Calcium builds strong bones.

questions.question: What is a balanced diet?
questions.correctAnswer: Eating a variety of foods in the right amounts for your needs
distractors: Eating the same food every day
questions.explanation: A balanced diet includes foods from all groups in proper proportions.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Balance means variety in the right amounts.

questions.question: What is the best time to eat before exercise?
questions.correctAnswer: About 1 to 3 hours before, with carbs and some protein
questions.explanation: Eating 1 to 3 hours before exercise gives fuel without stomach discomfort.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fuel up one to three hours before exercise.

questions.question: How many minutes of physical activity should teens get each day?
questions.correctAnswer: At least 60 minutes
questions.explanation: Health guidelines recommend at least 60 minutes of physical activity daily for teens.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sixty minutes a day keeps teens healthy.

questions.question: What is aerobic exercise?
questions.correctAnswer: Exercise that raises heart rate and uses oxygen, like running or swimming
questions.explanation: Aerobic exercise uses large muscles rhythmically and improves heart and lung fitness.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Aerobic exercise gets your heart pumping.

questions.question: What is the resting heart rate range for a healthy teen?
questions.correctAnswer: About 60 to 100 beats per minute
questions.explanation: A normal resting heart rate for teens is roughly 60 to 100 beats per minute.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Resting heart rate is usually 60 to 100.

questions.question: What does warming up before exercise do?
questions.correctAnswer: It prepares muscles and reduces injury risk
questions.explanation: Warming up raises blood flow and loosens muscles before harder activity.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Warm up to protect your muscles.

questions.question: What is the purpose of cooling down after exercise?
questions.correctAnswer: To gradually lower heart rate and prevent dizziness
questions.explanation: Cooling down lets your heart rate and breathing return to normal gradually.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cool down to let your body settle.

questions.question: What is flexibility?
questions.correctAnswer: The ability of joints to move through their full range of motion
questions.explanation: Flexibility is how far joints can move, improved by stretching.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Flexibility is how far your joints can move.

questions.question: What is muscular strength?
questions.correctAnswer: The maximum force a muscle can produce in one effort
distractors: How long a muscle can work
questions.explanation: Muscular strength is the most force a muscle can exert at once.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Strength is max force in one effort.

questions.question: What is muscular endurance?
questions.correctAnswer: The ability of muscles to work repeatedly without tiring
distractors: The maximum force in one lift
questions.explanation: Muscular endurance is how long muscles can keep working.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Endurance is lasting power.

questions.question: What is the target heart rate zone for moderate exercise?
questions.correctAnswer: About 50 to 70 percent of maximum heart rate
questions.explanation: Moderate exercise targets about 50 to 70 percent of your maximum heart rate.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Moderate exercise is 50 to 70 percent of max.

questions.question: What is maximum heart rate roughly calculated as?
questions.correctAnswer: 220 minus your age
questions.explanation: Maximum heart rate is often estimated as 220 minus age.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Max heart rate is about 220 minus your age.

questions.question: What is the FITT principle?
questions.correctAnswer: Frequency, Intensity, Time, and Type of exercise
questions.explanation: FITT stands for Frequency, Intensity, Time, and Type, the parts of a workout plan.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: FITT is frequency, intensity, time, type.

questions.question: What is the best way to prevent sports injuries?
questions.correctAnswer: Warm up, use proper technique, and wear protective gear
questions.explanation: Proper warm-up, technique, rest, and gear reduce injury risk.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Warm up, use good form, wear gear.

questions.question: What is the RICE method for injuries?
questions.correctAnswer: Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation
questions.explanation: RICE stands for Rest, Ice, Compression, and Elevation for soft tissue injuries.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: RICE is rest, ice, compression, elevation.

questions.question: How many days per week should teens do muscle-strengthening activities?
questions.correctAnswer: At least 3 days per week
questions.explanation: Guidelines recommend muscle-strengthening activities at least 3 days a week.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Strength training three days a week.

questions.question: What is body composition?
questions.correctAnswer: The proportion of fat and lean tissue in the body
questions.explanation: Body composition is the ratio of fat mass to lean mass like muscle and bone.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Body composition is fat versus lean tissue.

questions.question: What is BMI?
questions.correctAnswer: A ratio of weight to height used to screen for weight categories
questions.explanation: BMI, body mass index, compares weight to height as a screening tool.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: BMI compares weight to height.

questions.question: Why is rest important in a fitness plan?
questions.correctAnswer: Muscles recover and grow stronger during rest
questions.explanation: Recovery days let muscles repair and adapt, preventing overuse injuries.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Rest is when muscles rebuild.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay hydrated during exercise?
questions.correctAnswer: Drink water before, during, and after activity
questions.explanation: Drinking water throughout exercise replaces sweat losses.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sip water before, during, and after.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of regular exercise for the brain?
questions.correctAnswer: Better mood, memory, and focus
questions.explanation: Exercise improves mood, memory, and concentration.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Exercise boosts mood and focus.

questions.question: What is a sprain?
questions.correctAnswer: An injury to a ligament from stretching or tearing
questions.explanation: A sprain injures ligaments, the bands connecting bones at joints.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A sprain hurts a ligament.

questions.question: What is stress?
questions.correctAnswer: The body's response to a demand or challenge
questions.explanation: Stress is how the body reacts to pressure, with physical and emotional changes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Stress is your body's alarm to pressure.

questions.question: What is a healthy way to manage stress?
questions.correctAnswer: Exercise, sleep, talking to someone, and relaxation
questions.explanation: Healthy coping includes exercise, rest, social support, and relaxation techniques.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Move, sleep, talk, breathe.

questions.question: What is anxiety?
questions.correctAnswer: A feeling of worry or fear that can affect daily life
questions.explanation: Anxiety is worry or fear that can become a problem when it is strong or lasting.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Anxiety is worry that will not quit.

questions.question: What is depression?
questions.correctAnswer: A persistent low mood and loss of interest lasting weeks or more
questions.explanation: Depression is a lasting low mood with loss of interest and energy, not just a bad day.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Depression is sadness that stays for weeks.

questions.question: What should you do if a friend talks about self-harm?
questions.correctAnswer: Take it seriously, stay with them, and tell a trusted adult immediately
distractors: Tell them to get over it
questions.explanation: Thoughts of self-harm need immediate help from a trusted adult or crisis line.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: If a friend talks about self-harm, get help right away.

questions.question: What is the US Suicide and Crisis Lifeline number?
questions.explanation: 988 is the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline in the United States.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 988 is the crisis lifeline.

questions.question: What is empathy?
questions.correctAnswer: Understanding and sharing another person's feelings
questions.explanation: Empathy means understanding what someone else feels.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Empathy is feeling with someone.

questions.question: What is a healthy relationship?
questions.correctAnswer: One built on respect, trust, honesty, and communication
distractors: One where one person controls the other
One where you never say no
questions.explanation: Healthy relationships feature mutual respect, trust, and open communication.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Healthy means respect, trust, and honesty.

questions.question: What is consent?
questions.correctAnswer: Clear, freely given agreement to do something
questions.explanation: Consent must be clear, voluntary, and can be withdrawn at any time.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Consent means a clear yes, freely given.

questions.question: What is bullying?
questions.correctAnswer: Repeated, intentional harm or intimidation with a power imbalance
questions.explanation: Bullying is repeated aggressive behavior where one side has more power.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bullying is repeated and one-sided.

questions.question: What is cyberbullying?
questions.correctAnswer: Bullying that happens online or through digital devices
questions.explanation: Cyberbullying is harassment through texts, social media, or other digital means.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cyberbullying is bullying through screens.

questions.question: What should you do if you are being cyberbullied?
questions.correctAnswer: Save evidence, block the person, and tell a trusted adult
questions.explanation: Save messages, block the bully, and report it to an adult or the platform.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Save it, block it, report it.

questions.question: What is peer pressure?
questions.correctAnswer: Influence from peers to act or think a certain way
questions.explanation: Peer pressure is the influence of friends or classmates on your choices.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Peer pressure is friends pushing you to follow.

questions.question: What is a good way to resist negative peer pressure?
questions.correctAnswer: Say no clearly, suggest another activity, and walk away
questions.explanation: Assertive refusal, offering alternatives, and leaving are effective strategies.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A clear no plus a better plan works.

questions.question: What is self-esteem?
questions.correctAnswer: How you value and feel about yourself
questions.explanation: Self-esteem is your overall sense of self-worth.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Self-esteem is how you see yourself.

questions.question: What is mindfulness?
questions.correctAnswer: Paying attention to the present moment without judgment
questions.explanation: Mindfulness is focusing on the here and now, noticing thoughts without judging them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mindfulness is noticing the present moment.

questions.question: How much sleep do teens need each night?
questions.correctAnswer: 8 to 10 hours
questions.explanation: Teens need 8 to 10 hours of sleep for growth, learning, and health.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Teens need 8 to 10 hours of sleep.

questions.question: What does sleep do for learning?
questions.correctAnswer: It helps consolidate memories and improve focus
questions.explanation: Sleep helps the brain store memories and stay focused the next day.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sleep locks in what you learned.

questions.question: What is a growth mindset?
questions.correctAnswer: Believing abilities can improve with effort and learning
questions.explanation: A growth mindset holds that effort and practice can grow your abilities.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A growth mindset says you can get better.

questions.question: What is emotional intelligence?
questions.correctAnswer: The ability to recognize, understand, and manage emotions
questions.explanation: Emotional intelligence is understanding your own and others' feelings and managing them well.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Emotional intelligence is knowing feelings and handling them.

questions.question: What is the legal drinking age in the United States?
questions.explanation: The legal drinking age is 21 in all US states.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The drinking age is 21.

questions.question: What is the main effect of nicotine?
questions.correctAnswer: It is addictive and stimulates the nervous system
questions.explanation: Nicotine is the addictive chemical in tobacco that raises heart rate and blood pressure.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nicotine is the addictive part of tobacco.

questions.question: What is the main risk of vaping?
questions.correctAnswer: Nicotine addiction and lung damage
questions.explanation: Vaping exposes lungs to nicotine and chemicals that can cause serious lung injury.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Vaping can damage lungs and addict you.

questions.question: What is the main effect of alcohol on the brain?
questions.correctAnswer: It slows brain function and impairs judgment
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant that slows the brain, impairing judgment and coordination.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Alcohol slows the brain and clouds judgment.

questions.question: What is binge drinking?
questions.correctAnswer: Drinking a large amount of alcohol in a short time
questions.explanation: Binge drinking is typically 4 to 5 or more drinks within about two hours.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Binge drinking is a lot, fast.

questions.question: What is the most common sexually transmitted infection in US teens?
questions.correctAnswer: HPV (human papillomavirus)
questions.explanation: HPV is the most common STI, and a vaccine can prevent the types that cause cancer.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: HPV is the most common STI, and there is a vaccine.

questions.question: What is the best way to prevent STIs?
questions.correctAnswer: Abstinence, or consistent and correct condom use
questions.explanation: Abstinence is the only sure prevention; condoms greatly reduce risk when used correctly.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Condoms and abstinence are the best protection.

questions.question: What is HIV?
questions.correctAnswer: A virus that attacks the immune system
questions.explanation: HIV infects immune cells and, untreated, can lead to AIDS.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: HIV attacks the immune system.

questions.question: What is the difference between a virus and a bacterium?
questions.correctAnswer: Viruses need a host cell to reproduce; bacteria can reproduce on their own
distractors: Bacteria need a host; viruses do not
questions.explanation: Bacteria are single cells that can live independently; viruses must infect host cells.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bacteria live alone, viruses need a host.

questions.question: Why do antibiotics not work on colds?
questions.correctAnswer: Colds are caused by viruses, and antibiotics kill bacteria
questions.explanation: Antibiotics target bacteria, so they do nothing against viral colds.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Antibiotics fight bacteria, not viruses.

questions.question: What is a vaccine?
questions.correctAnswer: A substance that trains the immune system to fight a disease
questions.explanation: Vaccines expose the immune system to a harmless form of a germ so it can respond fast later.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Vaccines teach your immune system.

questions.question: What is herd immunity?
questions.correctAnswer: Protection of a community when enough people are immune
distractors: Immunity from one person to another
questions.explanation: When enough people are immune, diseases cannot spread easily, protecting those who cannot be vaccinated.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: When most are immune, everyone is safer.

questions.question: What is the first step in treating a minor cut?
questions.correctAnswer: Clean it with soap and water
questions.explanation: Wash a minor cut with soap and water, then cover it with a clean bandage.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Clean it first, then cover it.

questions.question: What should you do for a nosebleed?
questions.correctAnswer: Lean forward and pinch the soft part of the nose
distractors: Lean back and tilt your head
Put ice on your neck only
questions.explanation: Leaning forward and pinching the nose helps a nosebleed stop.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Lean forward and pinch for a nosebleed.

questions.question: What is the first thing to do if someone is choking and cannot speak?
questions.correctAnswer: Give abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver)
questions.explanation: If a person cannot speak or cough, abdominal thrusts can dislodge the blockage.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: If they cannot speak, do abdominal thrusts.

questions.question: What is CPR?
questions.correctAnswer: Chest compressions and rescue breaths to keep blood flowing when the heart stops
questions.explanation: CPR uses chest compressions to circulate blood when someone's heart has stopped.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: CPR keeps blood moving when the heart stops.

questions.question: What number do you call for emergencies in the US?
questions.explanation: 911 is the US emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 911 is the emergency number.

questions.question: What is the best first aid for a minor burn?
questions.correctAnswer: Cool it with running water
questions.explanation: Cool a minor burn under running water, then cover it loosely.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cool a burn with running water.

questions.question: What is the main cause of skin cancer?
questions.correctAnswer: Ultraviolet radiation from the Sun
questions.explanation: UV radiation damages skin cells and is the main cause of skin cancer.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: UV rays are the main cause of skin cancer.

questions.question: What SPF should sunscreen be for good protection?
questions.correctAnswer: At least SPF 30
questions.explanation: Dermatologists recommend sunscreen of SPF 30 or higher, reapplied every two hours.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: SPF 30 or higher is the standard.

questions.question: What is the main way to prevent food poisoning?
questions.correctAnswer: Cook food to safe temperatures and wash hands
questions.explanation: Safe cooking temperatures, clean hands, and proper storage prevent most food poisoning.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cook it right and wash your hands.

questions.question: What temperature should a refrigerator be?
questions.correctAnswer: At or below 40 degrees Fahrenheit (4 degrees Celsius)
questions.explanation: Refrigerators should stay at or below 40 F to slow bacterial growth.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Keep the fridge at or below 40 F.

questions.question: What is the difference between a sprain and a strain?
questions.correctAnswer: A sprain injures a ligament; a strain injures a muscle or tendon
distractors: A strain injures a joint only
questions.explanation: Sprains affect ligaments at joints; strains affect muscles or tendons.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sprain is ligament, strain is muscle.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a seatbelt?
questions.correctAnswer: To keep you in place and spread crash forces across strong parts of the body
questions.explanation: Seatbelts restrain occupants and distribute crash forces, greatly reducing injury.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Seatbelts spread crash forces and keep you in place.

questions.question: What is the leading cause of death for US teens?
questions.correctAnswer: Unintentional injuries, especially car crashes
questions.explanation: Car crashes and other unintentional injuries are the top cause of teen deaths.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Crashes are the top killer of teens.

questions.question: What is the main risk of texting while driving?
questions.correctAnswer: It takes eyes, hands, and mind off the road
questions.explanation: Texting distracts visually, manually, and mentally, greatly raising crash risk.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Texting while driving is three kinds of distraction.

questions.question: What is the best way to protect your privacy online?
questions.correctAnswer: Use strong passwords, limit sharing, and check privacy settings
questions.explanation: Strong unique passwords and careful sharing protect your online privacy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Strong passwords and careful sharing protect you.

questions.question: What is a strong password?
questions.correctAnswer: A long mix of letters, numbers, and symbols, unique to each account
questions.explanation: Strong passwords are long, varied, and different for each account.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Long, mixed, and unique makes a strong password.

questions.question: What is the main function of the immune system?
questions.correctAnswer: To defend the body against germs and disease
questions.explanation: The immune system recognizes and attacks pathogens.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The immune system defends you from germs.

questions.question: What is the difference between type 1 and type 2 diabetes?
questions.correctAnswer: Type 1 is an autoimmune loss of insulin; type 2 is insulin resistance, often linked to lifestyle
distractors: Type 1 is caused by eating sugar
questions.explanation: In type 1 the body stops making insulin; in type 2 the body resists insulin's effects.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Type 1 makes no insulin, type 2 resists it.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce the risk of heart disease?
questions.correctAnswer: Exercise, eat well, avoid smoking, and manage blood pressure
questions.explanation: Regular exercise, a healthy diet, no smoking, and controlled blood pressure lower heart risk.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Move, eat well, do not smoke.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the skeletal system?
questions.correctAnswer: To support the body and protect organs
questions.explanation: Bones support the body, protect organs, and make blood cells.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bones support and protect.

questions.question: What is the function of the respiratory system?
questions.correctAnswer: To bring oxygen in and remove carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: The respiratory system exchanges gases between air and blood.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Breathing brings in oxygen and removes CO2.

questions.question: What is the main job of the kidneys?
questions.correctAnswer: To filter waste from the blood and make urine
questions.explanation: Kidneys filter blood and remove waste as urine.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Kidneys filter your blood.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid the flu?
questions.correctAnswer: Get a flu vaccine and wash hands often
questions.explanation: Annual flu vaccination and handwashing are the best flu prevention.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Flu shots and handwashing beat the flu.
